comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C6-C7, C30, C67-C73, C102 regarding FGFR inhibitor rescue experiments. Both evaluations find the evidence strongly supported. OpenEval notes sample sizes not explicitly stated; peer reviewers (R1, R3) describe the data as 'most convincing and exciting' with 'robust experimental evidence.'

Both address claims C61-C66 regarding GLI protein levels and SHH signaling independence. OpenEval finds evidence supported despite variability. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to unresolved discrepancy with Jiwani et al. (2020) regarding GLI2 levels - this study shows decrease while prior work showed increase. Reviewer 3 notes supplementary revisions don't fully resolve concerns.

Both address claims C33-C37 regarding FGF5 upregulation in infantile MBSHH from patient cohort analysis. Strong agreement on support. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (n=763, p-values); peer reviewers note Figure 1 'substantially improved' and extraction from patient samples as 'notable strength.'

Both address claims C44-C50 regarding Fgf5 expression and spatial correlation with GNP expansion. OpenEval finds evidence well-supported by multiple techniques. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to critical unresolved concern about identifying cell types secreting FGF5 and whether signaling is paracrine or autocrine - editors note 'current limitations' require future validation.

Strong agreement on claims C54-C60 regarding pErk1/2 staining and FGF signaling activation. Both find evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes quantification and statistical significance; peer reviewers (R1, R3) note data 'convincingly show' FGFR signaling drives GNP proliferation with 'robust experimental evidence.'

Both address claims C126-C129 regarding timing-dependent effects of hGFAP-Cre deletion. OpenEval finds evidence supported with acknowledged limitations about cell-type specificity. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting hGFAP-Cre targets multiple cell types and authors don't fully address neuron-glial interactions, though reviewer acknowledges authors' recognition of limitations.

Both address claims C76, C79 regarding DNA damage markers. OpenEval finds evidence supported though interpretation somewhat speculative. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to unresolved concern about proper controls for Cre-induced DNA breaks - control group mentioned in author response not present in revision.

Substantial overlap on claims C89-C97 regarding Sufu;Trp53-dKO tumor phenotypes and Fgf5 expression patterns. OpenEval finds evidence supported but notes C97 (Fgf5 'triggers' signaling) is correlative not causative. Peer review finds tumor formation experiments (C83-C88, C89-C97) supported without major concerns.

Both address claims C83-C88 regarding tumor formation in double mutants and two-hit model. Strong agreement on support. OpenEval notes number of animals not clearly stated and suggests longer follow-up. Peer reviewers accept the tumor formation data without raising concerns.

Both address therapeutic/translational claims C2-C3, C8, C31, C103-C104, C132-C134. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting claims extend beyond data and require validation in patients. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 2 states study 'appears incomplete,' conclusions 'overstated,' and question of whether FGFR inhibition prevents tumors 'remains untested.'

Both address mechanistic model claims C110-C111 regarding how SUFU regulates Fgf5. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting hypothesis not directly tested. Peer review also rates as UNCERTAIN, with confidence undermined by unresolved discrepancy about GLI2 levels between this study and prior work.

Partial overlap on claims C40-C43 regarding Pax6+ cell expansion and morphological observations. OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence supported (C40-C50). Peer review addresses subset (C40-C43) and finds morphological observations supported without concerns.

Both address claim C109 regarding synthesis of findings into coherent model. OpenEval finds model supported by spatial/temporal correlations but notes mechanistic details unclear. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete establishment of causal relationships and need for future validation.

OpenEval addresses claims C105-C107 regarding SUFU's non-canonical functions and regulation of FGF signaling in regions with low SHH activity. Rated as UNCERTAIN with C107 explicitly speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval addresses claims C112-C116 regarding Fgf5 expression patterns in normal development and functional role. Finds evidence supported by citations and reasonable inferences, though functional role not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval addresses claims C117-C119 regarding context-dependent FGF signaling differences and comparison with other studies. Finds evidence supported by citations and Western blot data, with C119 speculative but reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C118 appears in peer R5 regarding GLI protein data.

OpenEval addresses claims C1, C9-C26 representing established background knowledge with appropriate citations. Finds all supported as necessary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers don't separately evaluate background claims.

OpenEval addresses claims C32, C39, C51-C53, C80, C108, C120-C124 regarding FGF signaling biology background from prior literature. Finds all supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers don't separately evaluate literature-based background claims.
